subject.title: RFC 0014: Pluggable scheduler seam in gateway

question: Should this RFC repository accept a new `kind: scheduler` / `owns: scheduled-jobs` plugin-SDK contract as the direction for external scheduled-job ownership?
rationale: The PR is a design RFC for new plugin API and gateway ownership semantics; the remaining question is not a mechanical docs fix and cannot be safely decided by cleanup automation.

options.title: Accept the RFC direction
options.body: Merge the RFC as the approved design and require the documented implementation issue, explicit config opt-in, Cron fallback proof, and run-state trust-boundary proof before runtime code lands.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Keep the PR open and ask the author to reduce or reshape the scheduler API, ownership token, or run-state event surface before merge.

options.title: Reject core scheduler ownership
options.body: Close or redirect the idea if maintainers want external schedulers to remain behind public HTTP/plugin surfaces without a first-class gateway ownership seam.

recommendation.title: Accept the RFC direction
recommendation.body: Merge the RFC as the approved design and require the documented implementation issue, explicit config opt-in, Cron fallback proof, and run-state trust-boundary proof before runtime code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest history-backed owner of the RFC process conventions on current main; product approval may still require OpenClaw gateway/plugin owners outside this repository.
